# pip-audit baseline. Two categories live here, both annotated:
#
# (A) Fixable, pending bump — a fix IS released upstream; ignored only
#     until Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml) PRs the bump. Workflow:
#       1. Dependabot opens a PR bumping the package.
#       2. PR lands → uv.lock has the fix version.
#       3. Remove the corresponding line(s) from this file.
#       4. CI now blocks any regression below that fix version.
#     These entries MUST name the package and fix version.
#
# (B) No upstream fix available — accepted risk. The advisory has NO
#     fixed version in OSV/PYSEC (pip-audit reports an empty Fix Versions
#     column; OSV lists no fixed range). The package is already at its
#     latest release, or no fixed release exists. These are kept until a
#     fix is published, then removed. Each entry MUST name the package and
#     why the residual risk is accepted.
#
# Never add a CVE here without a comment. For category (A), never add one
# to make the build green without a tracking issue / PR.
#
# Format: one vulnerability id (CVE-… or PYSEC-…) per line, as pip-audit
# reports it; lines starting with '#' and blank lines are ignored.
#
# ===== Baseline is currently empty =====
#
# `uv lock --upgrade` on 2026-09-18 brought every dependency current;
# `pip-audit` (no ignores) reports zero known vulnerabilities, including
# the packages previously listed under category (B) as having no fix
# (markdown, ollama, pyjwt, torch, transformers) — fixes have since
# shipped for all of them. Re-populate this file the next time `pip-audit`
# finds a fixable CVE that can't be bumped away immediately.
